tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not only she arrived late, but she also forgot her keys.
Seldom the café opens before seven on Sundays.
Never the neighbours had complained about the noise.
No sooner had the kettle boiled than the toast burned.
Under no circumstances the children will stay home alone.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Not only she arrived late, but she also forgot her keys.**

Not only opens the sentence, so English expects question-style order after it. Here she arrived keeps ordinary subject-verb order, which is the wrong shape after a fronted restrictive phrase. Insert do-support: Not only did she arrive late, but she also forgot her keys.

Mark it wrong and prefer "Not only did she arrive late, but she also forgot her keys."
**B) Seldom the café opens before seven on Sundays.**

Seldom is a frequency negative, and when it sits first it should trigger inversion. The café follows immediately with no auxiliary before it, so the line still reads as everyday subject-verb order. For present simple, invent does and keep the base verb: Seldom does the café open before seven on Sundays.

That opener fails without do-support — rewrite as "Seldom does the café open before seven on Sundays."
**C) Never the neighbours had complained about the noise.**

Never is fronted, but the neighbours still comes before had. With past perfect the auxiliary must move left of the subject while the past participle stays after it. The cleaned order is Never had the neighbours complained about the noise.

Reject this line; the clean past-perfect swap is "Never had the neighbours complained about the noise."
**D) No sooner had the kettle boiled than the toast burned.**

No sooner already shows the classic past-perfect swap: had sits before the kettle. The correlative than (not when) correctly links the second event. Both the inversion and the linker are in place, so the kettle-and-toast line stands.

Keep this: no sooner already puts had before the subject and pairs with than.
**E) Under no circumstances the children will stay home alone.**

Under no circumstances is a stock negative fronting phrase, so the next word should be a modal. Instead the children precedes will, which leaves ordinary statement order after the opener. Pull the modal forward: Under no circumstances will the children stay home alone.

That fails — pull the modal forward: "Under no circumstances will the children stay home alone."
tasks.solution_overview:
These five lines open with negative or restrictive fronts: not only, seldom, never, no sooner, under no circumstances. The everyday scenes (arriving late, café hours, noisy neighbours, a kettle, kids alone) are just the wrapper.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

When a negative phrase sits first, English usually flips auxiliary and subject - the same swap you use in questions. With past perfect, move had before the subject; with present simple, invent do/does; with a modal, move will/should/can forward. Also watch correlatives after no sooner (than, not when).

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Read left to right: if the first chunk is negative/restrictive and the next word is the subject, mark FALSE. If the auxiliary already precedes the subject, and any correlative is right, mark TRUE. Only one line here already shows the swap.

**Answer.** A=FALSE, B=FALSE, C=FALSE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 2
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Hardly had the film started when the fire alarm went off.
Rarely we see such clear skies in November.
Little did the guests realise how long the queue would be.
Not only did the recipe look simple, but it also tasted great.
Seldom the library stays open past nine on weekdays.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Hardly had the film started when the fire alarm went off.**

Hardly opens with past-perfect inversion already in place: had the film started. The second clause is linked with when, which is the right partner for hardly (not than). Word order and correlative both match the exam template.

Accept the line: hardly had… when… already shows the textbook inversion and linker.
**B) Rarely we see such clear skies in November.**

Rarely sits first, yet we follows at once with no auxiliary in between. Present simple has nothing to move, so you invent do and park it before the subject. The repair is Rarely do we see such clear skies in November.

Mark it wrong and prefer "Rarely do we see such clear skies in November."
**C) Little did the guests realise how long the queue would be.**

Little here means "not at all," so it behaves like a negative fronting word. Did the guests correctly places the auxiliary before the subject, then keeps the base verb realise. That is exactly the restrictive-inversion pattern exams expect.

That pairing is sound — little + did + subject is the restrictive pattern exams want.
**D) Not only did the recipe look simple, but it also tasted great.**

Fronted not only takes inversion, and did the recipe supplies it. The second half stays balanced with but… also, so the correlative pair is complete. Both order and linkage are clean.

This is sound: not only did… but also… inverts and balances cleanly.
**E) Seldom the library stays open past nine on weekdays.**

Seldom fronts a frequency negative, but the library stays in everyday present-simple order. You need does before the subject and the base verb stay after it. Rewrite as Seldom does the library stay open past nine on weekdays.

Reject this; rewrite as "Seldom does the library stay open past nine on weekdays."
tasks.solution_overview:
Task 2 drills the core set - hardly, rarely, little, not only, seldom - against everyday scenes (a film, November skies, a queue, a recipe, library hours). Some lines already invert; others leave plain subject-verb order after the front.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Hardly with past perfect wants had before the subject and when (not than) afterward. Rarely and seldom in the present need do/does. Little meaning "not at all" behaves like a negative front. Not only at the start needs inversion plus a balanced but also clause.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Spot the fronted trigger, then check the next word: auxiliary good, subject bad. For present simple with no auxiliary in sight, ask whether do/does should be invented. Mark TRUE only when that swap (and any correlative) is already there.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 3
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Under no circumstances should this door be left unlocked overnight.
No sooner the bus pulled away than Marta realised she had left her bag.
Never has the school cancelled sports day for such a light drizzle.
Scarcely the match had begun before the referee stopped play.
At no time the coach authorised a change of kit colour.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Under no circumstances should this door be left unlocked overnight.**

The policy opener under no circumstances correctly pulls the modal forward. Should this door be left reads like question order after the fronted phrase. Formal wording does not change the inversion rule, and the line already follows it.

Keep this: under no circumstances already parks the modal before the subject.
**B) No sooner the bus pulled away than Marta realised she had left her bag.**

No sooner is present, and than is the right correlative — but inversion is missing. The bus sits right after no sooner instead of had the bus. Move had left of the subject: No sooner had the bus pulled away than Marta realised she had left her bag.

That correlative fails — prefer "No sooner had the bus pulled away than Marta realised she had left her bag."
**C) Never has the school cancelled sports day for such a light drizzle.**

Never has the school cancelled… correctly inverts present perfect. Has precedes the subject; the past participle cancelled stays after it. That is the target never + perfect shape.

Accept the line: never + has + subject + past participle is already inverted.
**D) Scarcely the match had begun before the referee stopped play.**

Scarcely fronts the sentence, yet the match still comes before had. Like hardly and barely, scarcely with past perfect wants had + subject + past participle. Fix to Scarcely had the match begun before the referee stopped play.

Mark it wrong and prefer "Scarcely had the match begun before the referee stopped play."
**E) At no time the coach authorised a change of kit colour.**

At no time is a full negative fronting phrase, so the next word should be an auxiliary. The coach authorised keeps plain past-simple order, which fails the swap. Add do-support: At no time did the coach authorise a change of kit colour.

That order fails — rewrite as "At no time did the coach authorise a change of kit colour."
tasks.solution_overview:
Focus on stock fronting phrases - under no circumstances, no sooner, never, scarcely, at no time - in policy and school settings. The rule is blunt: if the negative phrase is first, the next word should be an auxiliary, not the subject.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Modal inversion after under no circumstances (should/will before subject). No sooner wants had + subject + than. Never + present perfect places has/have before the subject. Scarcely mirrors hardly (had + subject + when/before). At no time needs do-support or another auxiliary before the subject.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Underline the opener, then ask whether the immediate next word is auxiliary or subject. Fix missing had after no sooner/scarcely and invent did after at no time when the verb is past simple. Correct lines already show that swap.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 4
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only after the rain stopped did the picnic become possible.
Not until the train doors closed did Alex notice the wrong platform.
Hardly the hikers had reached the ridge when fog rolled in.
On no account may visitors feed the animals in this enclosure.
Nowhere in the guidebook does it mention the Monday closure.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Only after the rain stopped did the picnic become possible.**

Only after introduces a time clause that keeps normal order inside it. The inversion lands in the main clause: did the picnic become. That split — normal time clause, inverted main clause — is exactly what only after requires.

That works: only after… correctly saves the inversion for the main clause (did…).
**B) Not until the train doors closed did Alex notice the wrong platform.**

Not until works the same way: leave the time clause alone and invert what follows. Did Alex notice supplies the required main-clause swap. Nothing inside the not-until clause needed flipping.

Keep this: not until… did… inverts only after the time clause, as required.
**C) Hardly the hikers had reached the ridge when fog rolled in.**

Hardly is fronted, but the hikers still sits before had. Past-perfect inversion after hardly always places had before the subject, then the past participle. Repair: Hardly had the hikers reached the ridge when fog rolled in.

Reject this near-miss; the clean version is "Hardly had the hikers reached the ridge when fog rolled in."
**D) On no account may visitors feed the animals in this enclosure.**

On no account is from the same family as under no circumstances. May visitors correctly parks the modal before the subject. The formal prohibition already shows the expected question-style order.

This is sound — on no account + modal + subject already shows the swap.
**E) Nowhere in the guidebook does it mention the Monday closure.**

Nowhere in the guidebook is a negative place adverbial at the front. Does it mention places the auxiliary before the subject and keeps the base verb after it. That is the standard nowhere inversion pattern.

Accept the line: nowhere… does + subject is already in question-style order.
tasks.solution_overview:
Four of these already invert after only after, not until, on no account, and nowhere. The odd one out is hardly without had before the subject - everyday hiking and picnic scenes wrapped around the same mechanics.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Only after / not until: leave the time clause alone and invert the main clause. Hardly needs had + subject + when. On no account behaves like under no circumstances (modal before subject). Nowhere at the front wants does/do/did + subject.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

For only after / not until, ignore word order inside the time clause and check the main clause. For hardly and negative place adverbials, demand the auxiliary immediately after the opener. Mark FALSE only when that swap is missing.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=FALSE, D=TRUE, E=TRUE

tasks.title: Task 5
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: No longer does the bakery deliver to our street.
Barely had the concert begun when the lights failed.
In no way can the warranty cover water damage from floods.
Not only was the hotel full, but the next town was booked out too.
Seldom have we eaten such fresh bread from a roadside stall.
tactical_explanations:
**A) No longer does the bakery deliver to our street.**

No longer at the front forces present-simple do-support. Does the bakery deliver already invents that auxiliary and parks it before the subject. The base verb deliver follows cleanly, so the delivery line is a model true.

Keep this: no longer + does + subject matches the present-simple inversion template.
**B) Barely had the concert begun when the lights failed.**

Barely mirrors hardly and scarcely for past-perfect fronting. Had the concert begun places the auxiliary before the subject, and when links the blackout. Inversion and correlative both match the stock pattern.

That pairing is sound — barely had… when… is formed the exam way.
**C) In no way can the warranty cover water damage from floods.**

In no way belongs with under no circumstances and on no account. Can the warranty correctly pulls the modal forward after the restrictive opener. Warranty wording stays formal, but the grammar is ordinary modal inversion.

Accept the line: in no way already places the modal before the subject.
**D) Not only was the hotel full, but the next town was booked out too.**

Fronted not only with a be-verb inverts be itself — no extra do is needed. Was the hotel full shows that swap, and the second clause completes the contrast. Order and balance are both clean.

This is sound: not only was… plus a completing second clause is already clean.
**E) Seldom have we eaten such fresh bread from a roadside stall.**

Seldom with present perfect places have/has before the subject. Have we eaten already shows that frequency-negative perfect inversion. The past participle eaten stays after the subject, as expected.

Keep this: seldom have + subject + past participle already inverts past experience.
tasks.solution_overview:
Every sentence here is already inverted - bakery delivery, a concert blackout, warranty wording, a full hotel, roadside bread. Use this task as a clean model set of the stock triggers.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

No longer + present simple → does/do before the subject. Barely mirrors hardly (had + when). In no way pulls the modal forward. Not only with be inverts be itself. Seldom + present perfect places have/has before the subject.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Confirm the fronted negative, confirm the auxiliary sits next, then note the correlative (when / but also) where relevant. If every line already matches those templates, all five are TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=TRUE

tasks.title: Task 6
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: No sooner had the dishwasher finished than the sink filled again.
Rarely does a local team win away in such weather.
Not only the chef objected, but the waiters also complained.
Under no circumstances will pets be allowed in the exhibition hall.
Never the museum had displayed so many private loans at once.
tactical_explanations:
**A) No sooner had the dishwasher finished than the sink filled again.**

No sooner already inverts past perfect with had the dishwasher finished. Than correctly links the sink filling again — not when. Auxiliary order and correlative both lock into the classic trio.

That works: no sooner + had + subject + than is complete and correctly ordered.
**B) Rarely does a local team win away in such weather.**

Rarely fronts a frequency negative with no other auxiliary in sight. Does a local team invents do-support and parks it before the subject. Present-simple inversion is therefore already done.

Accept the line: rarely does + subject + base verb is the present-simple fix baked in.
**C) Not only the chef objected, but the waiters also complained.**

Not only is fronted, yet the chef objected keeps ordinary past-simple order. A matching but also clause cannot rescue missing inversion after the opener. Insert did: Not only did the chef object, but the waiters also complained.

Mark it wrong and prefer "Not only did the chef object, but the waiters also complained."
**D) Under no circumstances will pets be allowed in the exhibition hall.**

Under no circumstances correctly pulls will before pets. The passive be allowed stays after the subject in question order. Policy English loves this shape, and the grammar matches.

Keep this: under no circumstances will + subject already shows modal inversion.
**E) Never the museum had displayed so many private loans at once.**

Never opens the line, but the museum still precedes had. Past perfect after never needs Never had + subject + past participle. Move had left: Never had the museum displayed so many private loans at once.

That fails — rewrite as "Never had the museum displayed so many private loans at once."
tasks.solution_overview:
Three lines already invert after no sooner, rarely, and under no circumstances; two leave the subject right after not only / never. Mentally flip those into question order and the repair appears at once.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

No sooner + had + than. Rarely + do-support in the present. Fronted not only still needs did/does even when but also is present. Under no circumstances + modal. Never + past perfect → Never had + subject.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Scan for the opener; if the subject is glued to it, mark FALSE and insert or move the auxiliary. When the line already reads like a question after the front, mark TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=FALSE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 7
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Hardly had the snow melted when another frost arrived.
Little the tourists understood about the ferry timetable.
Only when the power returned did the fridge start humming again.
Scarcely had the paint dried on the fence when rain began.
Seldom the post office updates its holiday opening hours early.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Hardly had the snow melted when another frost arrived.**

Hardly had the snow melted already places had before the subject. When links the next frost — the right correlative after hardly, not than. Both halves of the pattern are present.

Accept the line: hardly had… when… is already textbook form.
**B) Little the tourists understood about the ferry timetable.**

Little as a fronting restrictor needs do-support before the subject. The tourists understood still reads as plain subject-verb order. Repair with did and a base verb: Little did the tourists understand about the ferry timetable.

Reject this; prefer "Little did the tourists understand about the ferry timetable."
**C) Only when the power returned did the fridge start humming again.**

Only when introduces a time clause that stays in normal order. Inversion begins after it ends: did the fridge start. Do not flip anything inside the when-clause itself.

That works: only when… did… rightly inverts the main clause alone.
**D) Scarcely had the paint dried on the fence when rain began.**

Scarcely had the paint dried mirrors the hardly/barely family. Had precedes the subject, and when seals the second event. The fence-and-rain line already matches the shared skeleton.

Keep this: scarcely had… when… is correctly formed and linked.
**E) Seldom the post office updates its holiday opening hours early.**

Seldom fronts the sentence, but the post office updates keeps present-simple order. Invent does, keep the subject next, and use the base verb update. Rewrite as Seldom does the post office update its holiday opening hours early.

Mark it wrong and rewrite as "Seldom does the post office update its holiday opening hours early."
tasks.solution_overview:
Hardly, scarcely, and only when are shown correctly; little and seldom are missing their auxiliaries. Everyday weather, tourism, power cuts, fencing, and post-office hours keep the focus on the grammar.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Hardly/scarcely + had + when. Little as a fronting restrictor needs did/does. Only when + clause, then invert the main clause. Seldom in the present needs does/do before the subject.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

For only when, wait until the time clause ends, then check the main clause. For little/seldom, invent did/does if none exists. Correlatives after hardly/scarcely should be when, not than.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not until the referee blew the whistle the players left the pitch.
Under no circumstances are bikes permitted inside the shopping centre.
No sooner had the oven preheated than the dough was ready.
At no point did the guide admit that the path was closed.
Rarely a quiet carriage stays quiet for the whole journey.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Not until the referee blew the whistle the players left the pitch.**

Not until correctly frames the referee’s whistle in a normal time clause. The failure is the main clause: the players left stays subject-first. Invert with did: Not until the referee blew the whistle did the players leave the pitch.

Trap: learners often leave the main clause untouched even when not until is fronted — the near-miss is ordinary past after a correct opener.

That order fails — prefer "Not until the referee blew the whistle did the players leave the pitch."
**B) Under no circumstances are bikes permitted inside the shopping centre.**

Under no circumstances with be inverts be itself. Are bikes permitted already shows that swap; no extra do-support is required. The shopping-centre ban is therefore grammatically clean.

This is sound: under no circumstances + are + subject is clean be-inversion.
**C) No sooner had the oven preheated than the dough was ready.**

No sooner had the oven preheated places had before the subject. Than matches no sooner as the correlative linker. Past-perfect inversion and than are both right.

Accept the line: no sooner + had + than is already complete.
**D) At no point did the guide admit that the path was closed.**

At no point behaves like at no time for fronting. Did the guide admit supplies do-support and parks the auxiliary before the subject. The path-closure admission is inverted correctly.

Keep this: at no point did + subject already places the auxiliary first.
**E) Rarely a quiet carriage stays quiet for the whole journey.**

Rarely opens a present-simple claim with no auxiliary moved or invented. A quiet carriage stays quiet keeps everyday order after the frequency negative. Add does: Rarely does a quiet carriage stay quiet for the whole journey.

Reject this; rewrite as "Rarely does a quiet carriage stay quiet for the whole journey."
tasks.solution_overview:
Most lines invert cleanly (under no circumstances, no sooner, at no point). The traps are not until without main-clause inversion and rarely without do-support - both classic exam misses in sports and travel wording.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Not until + time clause → invert the main clause only. Be-verb inversion after under no circumstances needs no extra do. No sooner + had + than. At no point + did. Rarely + present simple → does/do.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Separate time-clause order from main-clause order for not until. For be, invert be itself; for present simple after rarely, invent does. Mark TRUE when the auxiliary already sits before the subject.

**Answer.** A=FALSE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only by booking early can we secure seats near the stage.
No sooner had the parcel arrived when the courier rang again.
Not only did traffic jam the bridge, but the tunnel closed as well.
Under no circumstances should raw chicken sit on the worktop.
Never before has the festival sold out in a single morning.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Only by booking early can we secure seats near the stage.**

Only by booking early is a restrictive front with an -ing phrase. The main clause still must invert: can we secure shows that modal swap. Only by / only with / only through all behave this way.

That works: only by… can + subject correctly inverts the following clause.
**B) No sooner had the parcel arrived when the courier rang again.**

Had the parcel arrived looks perfect after no sooner, so the order scan can fool you. The linker is when, but no sooner always pairs with than. When belongs with hardly/scarcely/barely — swap it here.

Trap: correct had-inversion with the wrong correlative is a classic near-miss on mid-level papers.

Mark it wrong and prefer "No sooner had the parcel arrived than the courier rang again."
**C) Not only did traffic jam the bridge, but the tunnel closed as well.**

Not only did traffic jam the bridge already inverts with did. But… as well finishes the contrast in an acceptable parallel second half. Keep verb ideas balanced once the first half has inverted.

Accept the line: not only did… but… as well is inverted and complete.
**D) Under no circumstances should raw chicken sit on the worktop.**

Under no circumstances should raw chicken sit places the modal before the subject. Food-safety tone does not change the rule: expect should/must/will next after this opener. The inversion is already done.

Keep this: under no circumstances + should + subject already shows the modal swap.
**E) Never before has the festival sold out in a single morning.**

Never before behaves like never for present-perfect fronting. Has the festival sold out parks has before the subject and keeps the participle after it. Never before / never again follow that same perfect swap.

This is sound — never before has + subject + past participle is already inverted.
tasks.solution_overview:
Inversion is mostly done right across booking, traffic, food safety, and festival sell-outs. The subtle miss is the correlative after no sooner: word order can look perfect and still fail if than/when is swapped.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Only by + phrase still forces main-clause inversion. No sooner pairs with than, not when. Not only + did + but… as well. Under no circumstances + modal. Never before behaves like never for present-perfect inversion.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

First confirm the auxiliary sits after the front. Then, for no sooner lines, check the linking word even if had is correctly placed. A wrong correlative alone is enough to mark FALSE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=TRUE

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Hardly had the teacher finished speaking than phones started buzzing.
Not until the keys were found did the family leave the flat.
Seldom do neighbourhood shops stay open past midnight.
On no account the intern may unlock the storeroom alone.
Little did the runners know a shortcut waited behind the hill.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Hardly had the teacher finished speaking than phones started buzzing.**

Hardly had the teacher finished speaking already inverts past perfect correctly. The fail is the linker than — hardly takes when (or before), not than. Than is reserved for no sooner; swap it here even though word order looks polished.

Trap: perfect inversion with a borrowed no-sooner correlative is a high-yield exam miss.

That fails — rewrite as "Hardly had the teacher finished speaking when phones started buzzing."
**B) Not until the keys were found did the family leave the flat.**

Not until the keys were found leaves the time clause in normal order. Did the family leave supplies the main-clause inversion that follows. That split is the whole not-until rule.

Keep this: not until… did… inverts only the main clause, as taught.
**C) Seldom do neighbourhood shops stay open past midnight.**

Seldom do neighbourhood shops stay invents do-support for present simple. Frequency negatives need do/does/did when no other auxiliary exists, and do is already here. The midnight-opening claim is therefore clean.

Accept the line: seldom do + subject + base verb is already present-simple inversion.
**D) On no account the intern may unlock the storeroom alone.**

On no account fronts a prohibition, so the modal should come next. The intern may still keeps subject before may. Move the modal: On no account may the intern unlock the storeroom alone.

Trap: on no account looks formal enough that subject-modal order can feel "written," but it fails the inversion test.

Reject this near-miss; prefer "On no account may the intern unlock the storeroom alone."
**E) Little did the runners know a shortcut waited behind the hill.**

Little did the runners know is the stock restrictive template. Little meaning "not at all" fronts like a negative and takes did + subject + base verb. The shortcut line matches that pattern exactly.

That pairing is sound — little did + subject + base verb is the restrictive pattern.
tasks.solution_overview:
Two errors mix correlative choice (hardly… than) with missing modal inversion (on no account). Everyday classroom, keys, shops, storerooms, and runners - judge both word order and the linking word after the fronted phrase.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Hardly pairs with when, not than - even when had is correctly inverted. Not until + clause → did in the main clause. Seldom + do. On no account requires the modal before the subject. Little did… is the stock restrictive shape.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

For hardly lines that already invert, still audit when vs than. For on no account, demand modal-subject swap. Mark TRUE only when both order and correlative (if any) are right.

**Answer.** A=FALSE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

tasks.title: Task 11
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only after the laundry dried the sheets were folded and stacked.
Nowhere else will you find cherries this sweet in late summer.
Scarcely had the guests sat down when dessert appeared.
Not only did the app crash, it also wiped the draft message.
Under no circumstances the cleaner will mix bleach with ammonia.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Only after the laundry dried the sheets were folded and stacked.**

Only after the laundry dried is a normal time clause — leave it alone. The main clause the sheets were folded stays subject-first, so be never inverted. Flip the main clause: Only after the laundry dried were the sheets folded and stacked.

Trap: only after can look finished once the time clause is written, while the main clause still lacks inversion.

Mark it wrong and prefer "Only after the laundry dried were the sheets folded and stacked."
**B) Nowhere else will you find cherries this sweet in late summer.**

Nowhere else at the front always inverts the following clause. Will you find parks the modal right after the place adverbial. Nowhere / nowhere else share that same swap.

Keep this: nowhere else will + subject already parks the modal before the subject.
**C) Scarcely had the guests sat down when dessert appeared.**

Scarcely had the guests sat down places had before the subject. When links dessert — the right correlative for scarcely. Inversion and linker both match the hardly family.

Accept the line: scarcely had… when… is correctly inverted and paired.
**D) Not only did the app crash, it also wiped the draft message.**

Not only did the app crash correctly invents did after the fronted correlative. It also wiped the draft stays parallel enough to finish the contrast. The first-half inversion is the decisive check, and it passes.

This is sound: not only did… with a parallel it also… clause already works.
**E) Under no circumstances the cleaner will mix bleach with ammonia.**

Under no circumstances opens the cleaning rule, so a modal should follow. The cleaner will mixes subject-before-will order after the front. Pull will forward: Under no circumstances will the cleaner mix bleach with ammonia.

Trap: the safety content sounds careful while the word order after the opener is still ordinary.

That order fails — rewrite as "Under no circumstances will the cleaner mix bleach with ammonia."
tasks.solution_overview:
Only after and under no circumstances still trap people who invert late or not at all. The other three already show the target shapes - nowhere else, scarcely, not only - for laundry, cherries, dessert, apps, and cleaning rules.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Only after + time clause → invert the main clause (were/did before subject). Nowhere else + will. Scarcely had… when…. Not only did… with a continuing second clause. Under no circumstances + will before the subject.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

After only after, jump to the main clause and reject subject-first order. After under no circumstances, reject subject before the modal. Use the three correct lines as anchors for the target shapes.

**Answer.** A=FALSE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 12
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: No sooner had the curtains opened than applause filled the hall.
Rarely have gardens recovered so quickly after a late frost.
Not only was the suitcase heavy, but the zip was broken.
At no time were passengers told about the platform change.
Barely had the bakery opened when the first queue formed.
tactical_explanations:
**A) No sooner had the curtains opened than applause filled the hall.**

No sooner had the curtains opened than applause filled the hall is a model line. Had precedes the subject, and than — never when — links the applause. Treat the correlative as automatic once the inversion is locked.

Keep this: no sooner + had + than is perfectly formed.
**B) Rarely have gardens recovered so quickly after a late frost.**

Rarely have gardens recovered inverts present perfect after a frequency negative. Have sits before the subject; recovered stays as the past participle. That is the stock rarely + perfect template.

Accept the line: rarely have + subject + past participle already inverts experience.
**C) Not only was the suitcase heavy, but the zip was broken.**

Not only was the suitcase heavy inverts be itself after fronted not only. The but-clause keeps the contrast clear without needing do-support. With was/were, invert be and leave the second half parallel.

That works: not only was… but… is correctly inverted and continued.
**D) At no time were passengers told about the platform change.**

At no time were passengers told inverts be in a passive frame. At no time / at no point / at no stage are equivalent triggers for that swap. Passive voice does not cancel the inversion requirement.

This is sound — at no time + were + subject is clean be-inversion.
**E) Barely had the bakery opened when the first queue formed.**

Barely had the bakery opened when the first queue formed mirrors hardly. Had before the subject and when afterward are both required and both present. Barely equals hardly for inversion purposes.

Keep this: barely had… when… matches the shared past-perfect template.
tasks.solution_overview:
A clean model set: no sooner, rarely, not only, at no time, barely - curtains, gardens, luggage, platform announcements, bakery queues. If your own answers miss any of these shapes, rewrite the wrong ones to match these templates.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

No sooner + had + than. Rarely + present perfect (have/has + subject). Not only + was/were. At no time + were (be-inversion). Barely + had + when.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Every line should already show auxiliary before subject and the right correlative. Treat this task as a checklist: if anything fails that scan, you would mark FALSE - here none do.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=TRUE

tasks.title: Task 13
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only if the weather clears will the outdoor market go ahead.
The notice not only lists opening times but also warns about roadworks.
No sooner had breakfast ended than the day trip coaches arrived.
Hardly the ink had dried on the consent form when surgery was cancelled.
Under no circumstances are personal heaters permitted in the office.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Only if the weather clears will the outdoor market go ahead.**

Only if the weather clears leaves the conditional clause in normal order. Will the outdoor market go inverts the main clause after that clause ends. Fronted only if still triggers the same main-clause swap as only when.

Accept the line: only if… will + subject correctly inverts the main clause.
**B) The notice not only lists opening times but also warns about roadworks.**

Here not only sits mid-sentence after the notice, not at the front. Mid-clause not only… but also keeps ordinary subject-verb order; inversion is not required. Lists and warns already show that normal pairing correctly.

**Tip:** Invert only when not only is fronted; mid-clause not only stays uninverted.

That works: mid-sentence not only… but also needs no inversion, and this line is fine.
**C) No sooner had breakfast ended than the day trip coaches arrived.**

No sooner had breakfast ended than the coaches arrived already inverts past perfect. Than is present and correct after no sooner. Confirm that linker every time — it is right here.

Keep this: no sooner + had + than is already complete.
**D) Hardly the ink had dried on the consent form when surgery was cancelled.**

Hardly fronts the consent-form line, but the ink still precedes had. Past perfect after hardly must place had before the subject, then the participle. Repair: Hardly had the ink dried on the consent form when surgery was cancelled.

Trap: when is correct, so the correlative looks fine while the missing had-before-subject is the real fail.

Mark it wrong and prefer "Hardly had the ink dried on the consent form when surgery was cancelled."
**E) Under no circumstances are personal heaters permitted in the office.**

Under no circumstances are personal heaters permitted inverts be after the policy opener. Are precedes the subject; no extra do is needed with a be-main verb. Notices and office rules often use exactly this shape.

This is sound: under no circumstances + are + subject already shows be-inversion.
tasks.solution_overview:
The sophistication here is knowing when not to invert: mid-clause not only… but also is fine without a swap. The only hard fail is hardly without had-before-subject - markets, notices, coaches, consent forms, and office policy mixed together.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Only if + clause → invert the main clause. Mid-sentence not only… but also keeps normal order. No sooner… than with had. Hardly needs had before the subject. Under no circumstances + are (be-inversion).

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Ask first whether not only is fronted or mid-clause. Mid-clause → no inversion required. Fronted negatives → demand the auxiliary. Hardly without had before the subject is an automatic FALSE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

tasks.title: Task 14
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not until did the plumber fix the leak the floorboards were dry.
In no circumstances should leftover rice sit out overnight.
Seldom has a village fete drawn such a crowd in midweek.
No longer the tram line serves the old factory estate.
Only after did the museum reopen were tickets put on sale.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Not until did the plumber fix the leak the floorboards were dry.**

Did has been jammed into the not-until clause itself: Not until did the plumber…. The time clause must stay normal; only the following main clause inverts. Repair by restoring normal past in the time clause and inverting the main clause: Not until the plumber fixed the leak were the floorboards dry.

Trap: seeing did anywhere after not until can feel like "inversion done," but the auxiliary must sit in the main clause, not inside the time clause.

That fails — prefer "Not until the plumber fixed the leak were the floorboards dry."
**B) In no circumstances should leftover rice sit out overnight.**

In no circumstances should leftover rice sit pulls should before the subject. In / under no circumstances are interchangeable for this modal swap. The food-safety line already shows question order after the opener.

Accept the line: in no circumstances + should + subject is correctly inverted.
**C) Seldom has a village fete drawn such a crowd in midweek.**

Seldom has a village fete drawn inverts present perfect after a frequency negative. Has precedes the subject; drawn is the past participle that follows. Frequency negative and perfect auxiliary line up.

Keep this: seldom has + subject + past participle already places the auxiliary first.
**D) No longer the tram line serves the old factory estate.**

No longer opens the tram line claim, but the subject still comes next with no do-support. Present simple after no longer needs does/do before the subject and a base verb after it. Rewrite as No longer does the tram line serve the old factory estate.

Reject this; rewrite as "No longer does the tram line serve the old factory estate."
**E) Only after did the museum reopen were tickets put on sale.**

Only after did the museum reopen wrongly inverts inside the time clause. Keep Only after the museum reopened in normal order, then invert the main clause alone. The sale-of-tickets clause should lead with were: Only after the museum reopened were tickets put on sale.

Trap: same misfire as not until did… — auxiliary glued to the time clause instead of the main clause.

Mark it wrong and prefer "Only after the museum reopened were tickets put on sale."
tasks.solution_overview:
Advanced traps put the auxiliary in the wrong clause (not until / only after). Remember: the time or condition clause stays normal; the following main clause inverts. Also watch missing do-support after no longer.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Not until / only after: never put did inside the time clause - invert the main clause only. In no circumstances = under no circumstances for modal inversion. Seldom + present perfect. No longer + present simple → does/do.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

If you see Not until did… or Only after did… glued to the time clause, mark FALSE. Re-attach the auxiliary to the main clause. For no longer without does, invent do-support.

**Answer.** A=FALSE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 15
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not only did the soup burn, but the bread went stale as well.
Scarcely had the rehearsal ended than the costume call began.
Never again will the club host fireworks without a fire marshal.
Little does the neighbourhood appreciate how quiet the park becomes at dusk.
Under no circumstances the lifeguard may leave the pool unattended.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Not only did the soup burn, but the bread went stale as well.**

Not only did the soup burn correctly invents did after fronted not only. But the bread went stale as well finishes the contrast acceptably. But also and but… as well both work once the first half inverts.

That pairing is sound — not only did… but… as well is inverted and balanced.
**B) Scarcely had the rehearsal ended than the costume call began.**

Scarcely had the rehearsal ended already places had correctly. The fail is than: scarcely/hardly/barely take when, while than belongs with no sooner. Swap the linker even though the inversion looks exam-ready.

Trap: right had-order plus a no-sooner correlative is a polished-looking false.

That correlative fails — rewrite as "Scarcely had the rehearsal ended when the costume call began."
**C) Never again will the club host fireworks without a fire marshal.**

Never again will the club host places will before the subject. Never again / never before behave like never for inversion after the front. The fireworks rule already shows that modal swap.

Keep this: never again will + subject already shows modal inversion.
**D) Little does the neighbourhood appreciate how quiet the park becomes at dusk.**

Little does the neighbourhood appreciate invents do-support for present simple. Little meaning "not at all" fronts like a negative and takes does/do + subject + base verb. The dusk-park line matches the usual template.

Accept the line: little does + subject + base verb is the present restrictive pattern.
**E) Under no circumstances the lifeguard may leave the pool unattended.**

Under no circumstances fronts the pool rule, so a modal should follow immediately. The lifeguard may still keeps subject before may. Move the modal: Under no circumstances may the lifeguard leave the pool unattended.

Trap: may already feels careful and formal, which hides the missing modal-before-subject swap.

Reject this; prefer "Under no circumstances may the lifeguard leave the pool unattended."
tasks.solution_overview:
Inversion looks right on the scarcely line, but the correlative is wrong. Pair that check with the modal-order miss on under no circumstances - soup, rehearsals, fireworks, a quiet park, and pool safety.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Not only + did + but… as well. Scarcely takes when, not than. Never again + will. Little + does. Under no circumstances needs the modal before the subject.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Audit correlatives on scarcely/hardly/barely even when had is correct. Audit modal placement after under no circumstances even when the rest of the sentence looks polished. Either failure is enough for FALSE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 16
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only when the Wi-Fi returned did the online class continue.
No sooner the suitcase was packed than the taxi horn sounded.
At no stage were residents told about the water shut-off.
Rarely do we publish the newsletter without a photo gallery.
Not only the soundtrack disappointed; the plot disappointed too.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Only when the Wi-Fi returned did the online class continue.**

Only when the Wi-Fi returned keeps normal order inside the time clause. Did the online class continue inverts the main clause once that clause ends. Main-clause inversion only is the whole only-when check.

Keep this: only when… did… rightly inverts the main clause alone.
**B) No sooner the suitcase was packed than the taxi horn sounded.**

No sooner is followed by the suitcase was packed — subject right after the opener. After no sooner the next word should be was/were/had, not the subject. Invert: No sooner was the suitcase packed than the taxi horn sounded.

Trap: than is already correct, so the correlative can distract from the missing inversion.

Mark it wrong and prefer "No sooner was the suitcase packed than the taxi horn sounded."
**C) At no stage were residents told about the water shut-off.**

At no stage were residents told inverts be in the passive after a negative time phrase. At no stage / at no point / at no time are equivalent triggers. Were before the subject is exactly what the frame needs.

Accept the line: at no stage + were + subject is already be-inverted.
**D) Rarely do we publish the newsletter without a photo gallery.**

Rarely do we publish invents do for present simple after a frequency negative. There is no other auxiliary to move, so do before we is the required invention. The newsletter line already shows that shape.

That works: rarely do + subject + base verb is present-simple inversion done right.
**E) Not only the soundtrack disappointed; the plot disappointed too.**

Not only leads the sentence, but the soundtrack disappointed stays subject-first. Fronted not only still needs did/does/do before the subject even if a second half echoes the idea. Repair: Not only did the soundtrack disappoint; the plot disappointed too.

Trap: a parallel second clause ("the plot… too") can feel complete while the opener still lacks inversion.

That fails — rewrite as "Not only did the soundtrack disappoint; the plot disappointed too."
tasks.solution_overview:
Two failures omit inversion after no sooner and not only. The survivors show only when, at no stage, and rarely done properly - Wi-Fi classes, packing, shut-offs, newsletters, and soundtracks.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Only when + clause → did in the main clause. No sooner requires inversion of be/had immediately after it. At no stage + were. Rarely + do. Fronted not only needs did/does before the subject.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

If no sooner or not only is glued to a bare subject, mark FALSE and invent or move the auxiliary. Mirror the three correct lines for the working templates.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 17
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Not until the fridge was emptied the movers wheeled it downstairs.
Under no circumstances may allergy medication be shared between guests.
Seldom has a community garden produced such a crop of tomatoes.
Only by rearranging the furniture can the sofa fit through the door.
Hardly had the babysitter arrived than the toddler woke up crying.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Not until the fridge was emptied the movers wheeled it downstairs.**

Not until the fridge was emptied is fine as a time clause. The movers wheeled still keeps subject-verb order in the main clause. Invert with did: Not until the fridge was emptied did the movers wheel it downstairs.

Trap: a clean not-until opener can mask a main clause that never inverted.

Reject this near-miss; prefer "Not until the fridge was emptied did the movers wheel it downstairs."
**B) Under no circumstances may allergy medication be shared between guests.**

Under no circumstances may allergy medication be shared parks may before the subject. After this phrase, expect may/will/should next — and may is correctly placed. Policy English still follows ordinary modal inversion.

Keep this: under no circumstances + may + subject already parks the modal first.
**C) Seldom has a community garden produced such a crop of tomatoes.**

Seldom has a community garden produced inverts present perfect after the frequency negative. Has precedes the subject; produced is the past participle that follows. That is the standard seldom + perfect shape.

Accept the line: seldom has + subject + past participle is correctly inverted.
**D) Only by rearranging the furniture can the sofa fit through the door.**

Only by rearranging the furniture leaves the -ing phrase as written. Can the sofa fit then inverts the main clause with the modal before the subject. Only by / only with / only through all trigger that following-clause swap.

That works: only by… can + subject correctly inverts the main clause.
**E) Hardly had the babysitter arrived than the toddler woke up crying.**

Hardly had the babysitter arrived already inverts past perfect correctly. Than is wrong after hardly — the correlative must be when. A polished had-swap still fails if the linker is borrowed from no sooner.

Trap: top-band items often pass the order scan and fail only on when vs than.

Mark it wrong and rewrite as "Hardly had the babysitter arrived when the toddler woke up crying."
tasks.solution_overview:
Top-band items stay inside negative/restrictive inversion: not until, under no circumstances, seldom, only by, hardly. Judge each line by whether the auxiliary moved - and whether than/when is the right partner.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Not until → invert the main clause. Under no circumstances + may. Seldom + present perfect. Only by + -ing → modal inversion in the main clause. Hardly + had still fails if than replaces when.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Run two passes: (1) auxiliary before subject after every fronted trigger; (2) correlative audit on hardly/no sooner. A line can pass pass one and still fail pass two.

**Answer.** A=FALSE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 18
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Under no circumstances is smoking permitted near the playground.

tactical_explanations:
**A) Under no circumstances is smoking permitted near the playground.**

Under no circumstances is smoking permitted inverts be after the policy opener. Is precedes smoking; no extra do is needed when be carries the sentence. Use this as a clean be-inversion model.

This is sound: under no circumstances + is + subject is clean be-inversion.
**B) No sooner had the ferry docked than foot passengers streamed ashore.**

No sooner had the ferry docked than foot passengers streamed ashore is exact. Had before the subject and than afterward remain the gold standard. Both pieces are present.

Keep this: no sooner + had + subject + than is already complete.
**C) Not only were tickets refunded, but free drinks were offered as well.**

Not only were tickets refunded inverts were after fronted not only. The but… as well half completes the contrast with parallel passive ideas. With were/was, invert be and skip do-support.

Accept the line: not only were… but… as well is correctly inverted and paired.
**D) Seldom does a weekday market feel this crowded before noon.**

Seldom does a weekday market feel invents does for present simple. Frequency negative + does/do + subject + base verb is the everyday template. The crowded-market line matches it.

That works: seldom does + subject + base verb is present-simple inversion in place.
**E) Little did neighbours expect the street party to last past midnight.**

Little did neighbours expect is classic restrictive inversion. Little meaning "not at all" fronts like a negative and takes did + subject + base verb. Store the shape as a production model.

Keep this: little did + subject + base verb already shows the restrictive swap.
tasks.solution_overview:
All five are model answers across the core triggers - playground rules, ferries, ticket refunds, weekday markets, and street parties. Treat this task as a checklist of shapes you should be able to produce under exam pressure.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Under no circumstances + is (be). No sooner + had + than. Not only + were + but. Seldom + does. Little + did. Every line should already show the auxiliary immediately after the front.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Confirm each opener, confirm the swap, confirm any correlative. With no misses in this set, every statement is TRUE - store them as production models.

tasks.title: Task 19
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Only after the gym closed members were allowed to collect belongings.
Not until the vet confirmed the results did the owners relax.
Barely had the campsite been booked when a storm warning arrived.
On no account should unfinished cakes leave the kitchen counter.
Never the caretaker had unlocked every classroom before dawn.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Only after the gym closed members were allowed to collect belongings.**

Only after the gym closed is a normal time clause. Members were allowed still keeps subject-first order in the main clause. Invert be: Only after the gym closed were members allowed to collect belongings.

Trap: only after can look finished at the comma while the main clause never flips.

That order fails — prefer "Only after the gym closed were members allowed to collect belongings."
**B) Not until the vet confirmed the results did the owners relax.**

Not until the vet confirmed the results keeps normal order in the time clause. Did the owners relax supplies the required main-clause inversion. Time clause normal, main clause inverted — both halves are right.

Accept the line: not until… did… inverts only the main clause, as required.
**C) Barely had the campsite been booked when a storm warning arrived.**

Barely had the campsite been booked when… inverts had even in passive past perfect. When matches barely/hardly as the correlative. Been booked stays after the subject once had has moved left.

Keep this: barely had… when… is correctly formed even in the passive.
**D) On no account should unfinished cakes leave the kitchen counter.**

On no account should unfinished cakes leave parks should before the subject. On no account and under no circumstances share that modal-before-subject rule. The kitchen prohibition already follows it.

This is sound — on no account + should + subject already shows the modal swap.
**E) Never the caretaker had unlocked every classroom before dawn.**

Never fronts the caretaker line, but the caretaker still precedes had. Never + past perfect needs Never had + subject + past participle. Move had left: Never had the caretaker unlocked every classroom before dawn.

Trap: past perfect content is present, so the line can feel "advanced" while subject-before-had remains wrong.

Reject this; rewrite as "Never had the caretaker unlocked every classroom before dawn."
tasks.solution_overview:
Two lines forget to invert after only after and never. The others show not until, barely, and on no account in full working order - gym closing, vet results, campsite booking, kitchen rules, and dawn unlocks.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Only after + clause → invert the main clause. Not until… did…. Barely had… when… (including passive past perfect). On no account + should. Never + past perfect → Never had + subject.

**Part 2: How to decide.**

Jump to the main clause after only after / not until and demand the auxiliary first. After never + past perfect, demand had before the subject. Match the three correct templates to the two repairs.

**Answer.** A=FALSE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

tasks.title: Task 20
tasks.context: Decide whether each sentence is grammatically correct as written.
statements: Nowhere in the hiking leaflet does it mention the Monday trail closure.
Not only did the hostel refill the kettle, but it also left fresh towels.

No sooner had the suitcases been labelled than the taxi pulled up.
tactical_explanations:
**A) Nowhere in the hiking leaflet does it mention the Monday trail closure.**

Nowhere in the hiking leaflet does it mention correctly inverts after a negative place adverbial. Does follows the nowhere phrase and precedes the subject. Nowhere / no place at the front always demand that auxiliary swap.

Accept the line: nowhere… does + subject is already in question-style order.
**B) Not only did the hostel refill the kettle, but it also left fresh towels.**

Not only did the hostel refill the kettle already invents did after the front. But it also left fresh towels keeps the second half parallel. Match verb forms across both halves of not only / but also — and both halves do.

Keep this: not only did… but also… is inverted and parallel.
**C) Hardly had the blackout ended when the street lights flickered back on.**

Hardly had the blackout ended when the street lights flickered back on is standard. Had before the subject and when afterward are both required and both present. Do not borrow than from the no-sooner pair.

That pairing is sound — hardly had… when… is correctly linked.
**D) Under no circumstances the landlord will enter without written notice.**

Under no circumstances opens the landlord notice, so will should come next. The landlord will still keeps subject before the modal. Final checklist on this opener: modal, then subject — Under no circumstances will the landlord enter without written notice.

Trap: legal-sounding under no circumstances… will enter can still fail if the subject sits before will.

Mark it wrong and prefer "Under no circumstances will the landlord enter without written notice."
**E) No sooner had the suitcases been labelled than the taxi pulled up.**

No sooner had the suitcases been labelled than the taxi pulled up closes the set cleanly. Passive past perfect still inverts had before the subject. Than after no sooner seals the correlative.

This is sound: no sooner had… than… is complete, including passive past perfect.
highlights: Nowhere in the hiking leaflet does
tasks.solution_overview:
Four model inversions and one classic miss: under no circumstances without modal-subject swap. Hiking leaflets, hostel service, blackouts, landlord notice, and labelled suitcases wrap the final checklist.

**Part 1: What to watch for.**

Nowhere… does…. Not only did… but also…. Hardly had… when…. Under no circumstances → will before the subject. No sooner had… than….

**Part 2: How to decide.**

If you catch the under-no-circumstances pattern every time - modal before subject - this topic is exam-ready. Use the four true lines as production models and fix the one order miss the same way.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE
